text:
mark: Heads up — after last night's CUDA driver roll in us-west-2 a bunch of TensorRT-backed models started failing to load on p4/dl1 nodes. Seen in canary and a handful of prod replicas.

anna: I saw OOM-ish errors in the engine builder logs, plus a few segfaults. Can you paste the error?

mark: paste: ```
TensorRT Error (engine.cpp:120): Failed to create engine
ERROR: NVINFER: nvinfer1::runtime::deserializeCudaEngine(): mismatch in libnvinfer API version (7.2.3 vs 8.0.1)
terminate called after throwing an instance of 'std::runtime_error'
  what(): TRT: failed to deserialize engine
Segmentation fault (core dumped)
```

rishi: hmm lib mismatch. The new driver shipped CUDA 12.2, and our packaged libnvinfer is built for 8.4/12.1 maybe. Also NCCL runtime warnings in the same timeframe.

emily: Also seeing FlashAttention kernels crash with illegal memory access on some sequences — stack traces point to xformers/flash_attn fused kernels. Might be changed PTX expectations after driver upgrade.

infra-oncall: Rolling nodes: we've drained 6 affected racks so far, but it cut capacity ~12% in us-west-2. Autoscaler hasn't fully caught up for high-throughput inference routes.

anna: Can we reproduce by booting a test node with the new driver and running a small TRT conversion + flashattn microbench? If yes we can try rebuilding TRT with the exact driver/toolkit or use compatibility flag.

mark: Repro steps I ran:
1) Start g4/p4 with vanilla AMI + driver 535.86
2) pip install tensorrt 8.6.1 wheel (bundled libnvrtc)
3) python convert.py -> fails at serializer

rishi: Quick mitigation: pin the driver back to 535.54 on the pool and rollback the canary. We did a hotfix policy to route traffic to older pool for latency SLOs.

deploy-bot: @mark rolled back driver pool "us-west-2-tensorrt-canary" to 535.54 at 2026-01-31T10:25:40Z :white_check_mark:

emily: For longer-term: we should produce a small compatibility matrix per model: (CUDA driver) x (libnvinfer) x (tensorrt wheel) x (xformers/flashattn). Right now it's implicit in our packaging and causing surprise.

anna: Agreed. Also let's add a CI job that runs the TRT serializer + flashattn unit with the major driver versions we support. Keep it short — 5 input shapes, one big batch, one long sequence.

rishi: NCCL note: some nodes log `NCCL WARN Call to ncclCommInitRank failed` after the upgrade, looks like drivers changed ibverbs behavior. That explains a couple of distributed hangs we saw. Reverting driver cleared the NCCL errors.

mark: Action items:
- infra: hold driver roll in other regions until compatibility matrix exists (infra-oncall)
- eng-runtime: add TRT+flashattn CI smoke (anna, rishi)
- infra: coordinate with vendor to get validated TRT builds for 12.2 (mark, infra-oncall)
- product: notify affected customers on the incident page about potential degradation in us-west-2 (emily)

infra-oncall: Acknowledged. I've paused multi-region driver deploys and set a blocking ticket. We'll also tag affected hosts as "kernel-compat-issue" for scheduling.

emily: Customer comm draft: short note, impacted inference nodes in us-west-2 experienced degraded availability due to a GPU driver upgrade that introduced compatibility issues with TensorRT and custom kernels (FlashAttention/xFormers). We're routing traffic and rolling back where needed. Will update with ETA.

mark: Thanks. If anyone captures a minimal repro snippet that triggers the TRT deserialize error, paste it here — that'll speed vendor debugging.

anna: I'll push a tiny repro script and artifact to S3 by EOD.

mark: Perfect. :thumbsup:
